Here's what I found regarding Google's Amber project, its VkScript command parser, and the related tokenizer/value handling components.

## Amber Overview

Amber is influenced by Talvos and VkRunner, and the VkScript syntax matches the format used by VkRunner. It is not an officially supported Google product.

Amber supports two script dialects. It can use scripts written in two dialects: AmberScript and VkScript, where the AmberScript parser is used if the first 7 characters of the script are #!amber, otherwise the VkScript parser is used.

## VkScript Parser & Command Parsing (relevant to `command_parser.cc`)

The specific file your query references (`src/vkscript/command_parser.cc`) is part of the VkScript parsing pipeline. The VkScript parser is broken into three major chunks: the Parser, SectionParser, and CommandParser. The Parser is the overall driver. The SectionParser breaks the input file into the overall chunks (each of the sections separated by the [blocks]). The CommandParser parses the [test] section specifically, while other sections are parsed directly in the Parser object.

## Number Tokenization (relevant to `GetValue`, `AsDouble`, float/double)

Your query touches on how numeric literals are tokenized and interpreted (integer vs. floating point). The AmberScript documentation explains this behavior: Literal numbers are normally presented in decimal form, and they are interpreted as integers or floating point depending on context — a command parameter is predefined as either integral or floating point, or the data type is user-specified (such as for buffer data). Additionally, whenever an integer is expected, you may use a hexadecimal number, which is the characters 0x followed by hexadecimal digits.

## A Relevant Command Parser Bug Fix

I found a pull request that directly modified `src/vkscript/command_parser.cc`. PR #268 "Vkscript: fix matrix stride bug" made 38 additions and 5 deletions in src/vkscript/command_parser.cc. The discussion involved matrix stride calculation logic: If it is std140 and the row size is 2, its stride will be 8, and the condition to check is use_std430_layout || type.RowCount() == 3U — meaning if std140 (use_std430_layout == false), it is true only when type.RowCount() == 3U.
